builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Ivern: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (1,139 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 51.3% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A jungle facilitator who frees camps and uses roots, shields and Daisy to create allied fighting space. Brush attacks provide a secondary offensive angle rather than changing his camp-clearing mechanic. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Redemption → Moonstone Renewer → Ardent Censer. Summon Aery keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Dawncore, Staff of Flowing Water.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Redemption → Moonstone Renewer → Ardent Censer, with Summon Aery.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Redemption → Moonstone Renewer → Ardent Censer) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 51.3% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Redemption → Moonstone Renewer → Ardent Censer.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

Passive: While in brush and for [3] seconds after leaving, Ivern's Attacks deal an additional [20 / 27.5 / 35 / 42.5 / 50 + (0.2) × AP] magic damage. Nearby allies will gain this effect for [1.5] seconds and deal [10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 + (0.1) × AP] magic damage.

Active: Ivern grows a patch of Brush, revealing the area for [8] seconds. The Brush persists until Ivern's team loses vision within it, or up to [45] seconds.

Ivern will not hurt non-epic monsters. Instead, Ivern can right click a monster to grow a Grove that costs [(characterLevelBreakpoints(start=15, perLevel=-0.882, changes=[])) × ((0.01) × Stat(12)[statFormula=1])] Health and [(characterLevelBreakpoints(start=20, perLevel=-1.175, changes=[])) × (0.01 × AbilityResource(default, statFormula=1))] Mana.

Groves: Grow over [(characterLevelBreakpoints(start=40, perLevel=-2, changes=[{"mLevel": 7, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": -3.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 12, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": -4.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 15, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": -2.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 16, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])) × (1)] second(s) Once fully grown, Ivern can harvest them, freeing the camp and earning gold and experience Ivern can also Smite the Groves to instantly grow and free the camp, earning gold and experience@SpellModifierDescriptionAppend@

Ivern summons his sentinel friend Daisy to leap into the fray for [45] seconds.

Daisy, Slam!: Daisy's 3rd consecutive Attack on the same champion or epic monster will launch a shockwave, dealing [90 / 140 / 190 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage to all enemies hit as well as Knocking Up for [1] second. This effect can only occur once every [3] seconds.

Recast: Instruct Daisy to Attack or move.

Ivern conjures a vine dealing [80 / 125 / 170 / 215 / 260 + (0.7) × AP] magic damage and Rooting the first enemy hit for [1.6 / 1.7 / 1.8 / 1.9 / 2] seconds. Allies that Attack a Rooted enemy dash into Attack Range. 

Recast: Ivern dashes directly onto the Rooted enemy.

Hitting non-epic monsters reduces {{ Spell_IvernQ_Name }}'s cooldown by 50%.

Ivern grants [75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 + (0.5) × AP] Shield to an ally champion or Daisy. After [2] seconds, it bursts, dealing [70 / 90 / 110 / 130 / 150 + (0.8) × AP] magic damage and Slowing enemies by [(0.4 / 0.45 / 0.5 / 0.55 / 0.6) × 100]% for [2] seconds.

If Triggerseed detonates and no enemy champions are hit while the shield still persists, the ally will be shielded for [75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 + (0.5) × AP] for [2] seconds.

builds.name: Brush personal carry
builds.summary: Test brush personal carry against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test brush personal carry against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Brushmaker grants Ivern's own attacks 0.2 AP magic damage for three seconds after leaving brush; Nashor and Dusk and Dawn emphasize that window. Rootcaller enables attack access and Triggerseed protects the approach; Daisy's independent slam supplies control rather than invented owner-item inheritance.
testPlan: Required state: Keep brush access and root a target before personal attacks.
Compare Ivern-only attack damage with Daisy commanded away.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Ivern's jungle passive cannot make this a normal monster-attack farming build.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Daisy is not assumed to carry Nashor, Rageblade or Spellblade from Ivern.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Guinsoo's Rageblade, Terminus, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Mobile bodyguard
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Ivern: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A jungle facilitator who frees camps and uses roots, shields and Daisy to create allied fighting space. Brush attacks provide a secondary offensive angle rather than changing his camp-clearing mechanic. Measure Daisy, shield timing and allied follow-up before testing brush-enhanced real attacks. AP/attack speed do not change the free-camp jungle mechanic into ordinary attack clearing. Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation.
builds.summary: Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation.
testPlan: Kit question for Ivern: Measure Daisy, shield timing and allied follow-up before testing brush-enhanced real attacks. AP/attack speed do not change the free-camp jungle mechanic into ordinary attack clearing.

Start with the early core (Support quest, movement/boots and Locket; Warmog only after its actual threshold) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use real support income and keep the quest/vision slot.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Ivern conjures a vine, dealing damage and rooting enemy targets hit. Ivern's allies can dash to the rooted target. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Warmog is a late threshold purchase, not in-combat regeneration or an assumed early spike.

The route fails Ivern's stated kit question: Measure Daisy, shield timing and allied follow-up before testing brush-enhanced real attacks. AP/attack speed do not change the free-camp jungle mechanic into ordinary attack clearing.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility. Also record allies lost while spending on personal damage.
tradeoffs: Warmog is a late threshold purchase, not in-combat regeneration or an assumed early spike.
Full cost 11,300 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Support quest, movement/boots and Locket; Warmog only after its actual threshold. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Begin with the actual support quest item; Celestial Opposition is earned by transformation, not directly bought as a 400-gold legendary. Keep buying vision.
Locket of the Iron Solari, Knight's Vow, Warmog's Armor are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.goal: Test daisy siege amplifier against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Daisy's third consecutive attack on one champion/epic monster creates a 0.5 AP magic shockwave with a three-second limit; Triggerseed bursts for 0.8 AP. AP and Bloodletter support those magic packets, while Cosmic Drive helps Ivern stay close enough to command and shield her.

Log Daisy attack/slam damage separately from E bursts and burn attribution.
